text:
Jori (CS): Quick alignment — I want a compact "concierge handoff" we can give customers at kickoff: focused on prefill + batching + streaming fallbacks. Main goals: reduce early churn, speed time-to-value, and surface renewal risks quickly. Thoughts?
Aria (AE): Love that. Can we make it a 1‑page checklist + a short email template the AE sends post-demo? Keep it actionable.
Devon (SRE): Yes. From infra side add clear knobs: warm_pool_size, prefill_parallelism, batch_size caps, and stream_fallback=true. Also the observability checks (cache hit header, p95 latency).
Maya (Eng-ML): Add an easy customer test to validate cache & streaming. Example curl + expected header:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: tenant-123" \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?stream=true
# Expect header: X-Redwood-Cache: HIT or MISS
```
Jori (CS): Draft runbook idea (short bullets customers can follow during first 48h):
- Day0: prefill top 10 intents, set warm_pool_size=2-4, enable streaming.
- Day0-1: monitor X-Redwood-Cache, p95 latency, error-rate.
- If cache MISS > 40% and p95 > 400ms -> increase prefill parallelism / enable adaptive batching.
- If streaming disconnects occur > 3 in 10min -> flip to non-streaming fallback route (route: low-latency variant) and open a support ticket.
Devon (SRE): Add recommended numeric defaults we can share with customers:
- Interactive/classic webchat: batch_size=1-4, target_p95=<=200ms.
- High-throughput ingest (txn): batch_size=8-32, target_p95=<=600ms.
- Prefill parallelism: 4 concurrent prefill workers for standard tenants.
Aria (AE): For renewal risk capture, propose a simple signal mapping we can include in the handoff: 
- Red flags within 14d: sustained p95 > threshold, >25% cache misses, repeated stream fallbacks, low engagement (<=10 queries/day).
- Action: CS check-in, enable extra warm capacity for 72h, schedule product training.
Maya (Eng-ML): Quick diagnostic snippet customers can run (python):
```
import requests
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', headers={ 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + TOKEN, 'X-Redwood-Tenant': 'tenant-123' }, json={ 'input': 'ping' }, stream=True)
print(resp.headers.get('X-Redwood-Cache'))
```
Jori (CS): I'll assemble the 1‑pager with the checklist + email template + the two snippets above. Plan: share draft in #customer-success in 24h. @Aria can you prototype the AE email? :thumbsup:
Aria (AE): On it. I'll include subject lines for low-touch vs high-touch customers and a short CTA to schedule a 30m optimization call.
Devon (SRE): I'll add the play for temporary scaling: how to request a 48h burst (internal ticket template to send ops). Also include the deploy check (example command):
```
# internal: enable prefill for tenant
POST /internal/tenants/tenant-123/prefill { "concurrency": 4 }
```
CS-Bot: Reminder created — "Concierge handoff draft" assigned to Jori, due in 24h.
Jori (CS): Great. Goal is to keep the customer-facing doc lean (one page) and an internal checklist (two bullets) for Ops. We'll run this on the next three pilots and capture feedback via a 5-question survey after day 7.
Aria (AE): Can we add one simple sample FAQ line about when we recommend turning on quantization/low-cost variants? I'll add it to the draft.
Maya (Eng-ML): Suggestion for FAQ: "If your p95 > 600ms and budget sensitivity is high, ask us about q4_8 quantized variants — expect 20-30% cost reduction, test for output drift."
Jori (CS): Perfect. Thanks team — I'll post draft soon. If anyone's got a short customer quote about the handoff working well, drop it here and I'll put it in the template.
